newsitem.title: USA: FDA rules aimed at curbing youth smoking.
newsitem.headline: FDA rules aimed at curbing youth smoking.

text.p: The tobacco industry, advertising and convenience store groups are asking a federal judge to throw out Food and Drug Administration regulations aimed at curbing smoking among children.
The groups argue that the FDA does not have the authority to regulate cigarette sales and marketing and that advertising restrictions violate free speech rights.
The following is a list of some of the key provisions of FDA regulations:
-- The banning of vending machines except in certain nightclubs and other places where people under 18 cannot enter.
-- The banning of billboards within 1,000 feet of schools and playgrounds.
-- Other billboards, outdoor and in-store advertising is limited to black-and-white text only, unless the ad is in a place that excludes people under 18 and is not visible from outside.
-- Print advertising with large youth readership (more than 15 percent or two million) limited to black-and-white text only.
-- The banning of brand-name sponsorship of sporting or other events. Only corporate name sponsorship permitted.
-- The banning of cigarette names on hats, T-shirts, gym bags and other products.
-- The requirement that retailers verify by picture identification the age of all tobacco purchasers who are under 27 years old.
